Chapter 9: Designing Your Own Dip Strategy
Now that you’ve got a real grip on what the dip is all about, let’s talk about what comes next—creating your own strategy to get through it.
Think of a dip strategy like having a map before you start a tough hike. Sure, it won’t magically flatten out the hills or remove every obstacle, but you’ll know what’s coming and how to prepare for it.
So, how do you put together a strategy that actually works for you?
First, try to spot the hurdles before you even reach them. Are you likely to face boredom, or maybe the sting of rejection? Will slow progress frustrate you, or could outside criticism throw you off? Jot down the specific challenges you expect. Just naming them takes some of their power away.
Next, set up regular check-ins with yourself. This might mean blocking out a few minutes every week to look back, see how far you’ve come, and ask if you’re still committed. Or maybe it’s meeting up once a month with a mentor who can keep you honest.
Here’s another piece—build rituals that help you bounce back. Little habits can make a big difference. Maybe it’s a daily walk, a few minutes of journaling, or just touching base with a friend who always lifts you up. These small acts keep your energy steady, even when things get tough.
And don’t forget to track your progress—visually. A simple chart, a journal, or even sticky notes on the wall can show you just how much you’re actually moving forward. Sometimes, seeing those little wins is all the motivation you need to keep going.
Let’s make it real with an example. Imagine a musician who’s learning a new instrument. They know they’ll probably get frustrated with slow improvement. So, what do they do? They plan for those tough moments, set up regular practice sessions, and keep track of every small win. That way, when they hit the dip, they’ve already got a system to help them push through.
At the end of the day, a well-designed dip strategy won’t promise you instant success. But it will boost your odds. Instead of just relying on sheer willpower, you’re turning the journey into a thoughtful process—one you can adjust as you go.
Over time, this approach doesn’t just get you through the dip. It actually builds your confidence and your skills, step by step.
